<b>Малая доза аспирина</b> (75–150 мг в: Low-dose aspirin (75–150 mg per day). A platelet has no nucleus — it cannot make new COX, so it produces no thromboxane for the rest of its life (7–10 days). Endothelial cells, which have nuclei, resynthesize COX within hours, so prostacyclin is largely preserved. A plug still forms at the site of a wound (ADP, thrombin), but a smaller one — and fewer clots form on plaques: this is how repeat heart attacks and strokes are prevented. Ibuprofen taken before aspirin occupies the COX channel and keeps aspirin from working. The price is bleeding and a risk of ulcers.
<b>Отмена аспирина.</b> Тромбоксан возвр: Stopping aspirin. Thromboxane returns gradually, as the bone marrow releases new platelets (about 10% per day). That is why it is stopped 5–7 days before elective surgery — if the risk of bleeding outweighs the risk of thrombosis (after coronary stenting, aspirin is usually not stopped).
\n <div><h2>Эйкозаноиды</h2>\n:
Eicosanoids

Derivatives of polyunsaturated C₂₀ acids (arachidonic, ω-6; eicosapentaenoic, ω-3). Prostanoids (prostaglandins, prostacyclin, thromboxanes) come from the cyclooxygenase pathway; leukotrienes and lipoxins from the lipoxygenase pathway; epoxides from cytochromes P450. They act through G protein–coupled receptors (EP1–EP4, IP, TP, BLT, CysLT), locally, and break down within seconds to minutes.

COX-1 and COX-2

COX-1 is constitutive (stomach, kidneys, platelets); COX-2 is inducible (inflammation: cytokines, endotoxin), but it is also present in the endothelium, kidneys and brain. The enzyme is bifunctional: cyclooxygenase (arachidonic acid → PGG₂) and peroxidase (PGG₂ → PGH₂).

Drugs

  • NSAIDs: aspirin (irreversible), ibuprofen, diclofenac, naproxen (reversible); coxibs are COX-2-selective.
  • Glucocorticoids act on phospholipase A₂ and the COX-2 gene.
  • Antileukotrienes: montelukast (CysLT₁ receptor), zileuton (5-LOX) — for asthma.
  • Prostaglandin analogs: misoprostol (stomach protection, obstetrics), latanoprost (glaucoma), alprostadil (keeps the ductus arteriosus open in newborns with duct-dependent heart defects; NSAIDs, conversely, close the duct).

Simplifications

  • The molecules follow their chemical formulas; the enzymes are schematic blobs, and the membrane and vessel are schematic.
  • Eicosanoid levels and platelet counts are a qualitative model; the time course after stopping aspirin is compressed.

<b>Мало кальция в пище</b>. Кишечник отд: Low dietary calcium. The intestine supplies less — calcium falls slightly and PTH rises (secondary hyperparathyroidism). Blood calcium stays almost normal, but the bones pay for it: their “account” gradually dwindles (the femur grows paler). This is how osteoporosis develops over years.
<b>Витамин D</b> — скорее гормон, чем ви: Vitamin D is more a hormone than a vitamin. In the skin, ultraviolet B breaks ring B of 7-dehydrocholesterol, giving previtamin D₃, which the warmth of the skin converts into cholecalciferol (D₃; it also comes from fish, eggs and supplements). The liver adds an OH at position 25, giving calcidiol (25-OH-D), the main circulating form; it is used to judge vitamin D stores (normal — from 30 ng/mL). The kidneys add an OH at position 1 — this is calcitriol, the active hormone. Its synthesis is switched on by PTH and low phosphate and switched off by calcitriol itself and FGF23; any excess is broken down by 24-hydroxylase (gray arrow).
Килограмм кальция лежит в костях, а в кр: There is a kilogram of calcium in the bones, but less than a gram in the blood. Parathyroid hormone and vitamin D make sure that gram does not shift by more than a few percent.
\n <div><h2>Обмен кальция и фосфата:
Calcium and phosphate metabolism

The body contains about 1 kg of calcium, 99% of it in bone as hydroxyapatite. Total plasma calcium is 2.2–2.6 mmol/L: almost half is bound to albumin, and the active fraction is ionized calcium (1.1–1.3 mmol/L). Acidosis increases the ionized fraction, alkalosis (for example, with hyperventilation) decreases it — cramps may occur.

Hormones

  • Parathyroid hormone (84 amino acids): bone — resorption via RANKL on osteoblasts; kidneys — Ca²⁺ reabsorption, phosphate excretion, calcitriol synthesis.
  • Calcitriol (1,25-(OH)₂-D₃): nuclear receptor VDR; in the intestine it switches on calcium-absorption proteins (TRPV6, calbindin), acts on bone and kidneys, inhibits PTH.
  • Calcitonin (C cells of the thyroid gland): inhibits osteoclasts.
  • FGF23 from bone promotes phosphate excretion and inhibits calcitriol synthesis.

Diseases

Hyper- and hypoparathyroidism, rickets and osteomalacia, osteoporosis, renal osteodystrophy, hypercalcemia of malignancy (PTH-related peptide, PTHrP).

Simplifications

  • Vitamin D molecules follow their chemical formulas; organs, cells and the bone surface are schematic.
  • Calcium and PTH levels come from a simple feedback model; the numbers are typical, not diagnostic.
  • Bone remodeling is shown thousands of times faster: a real cycle takes 3–6 months.
